tldr: Under the paper's explicit design restriction of predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete randomization within each growing block, past-only AIPW adjustments make centered block scores a martingale difference array, so cross-block covariance disappears without conditioning on the realized terminal path. The three adaptive contributions are the predictable complete-block transport envelope, its observable history-uniform plug-in theorem with deterministic rate bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n\), and conservative martingale Wald inference from the estimated upper endpoint. Supporting computation uses quantile sorting for two arms and a finite transportation program for fixed \(K\), while the worked \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) validation gives contrast-square costs zero and four by direct substitution. The static two-arm, regression-adjusted, and nonadaptive-stratified reductions are noncontributory validation checks attributed directly to their published sources. Ex ante completion sharpness is not claimed: the open problem separates single-node integrality from cross-history consistency and asks whether fixed-fraction undercoverage can be attained by one completion sequence whose entire induced triangular array remains in the common-overlap, residual-moment, arm-count, leverage, and nondegeneracy inference class.
gap: Li and Zhao's adaptive design-based AIPW theory permits arbitrary history-measurable joint block assignment laws with positive marginals and identifies a martingale covariance, but it neither supplies this paper's predictable fixed-count complete-block restriction nor characterizes the resulting sharp residual-coupling range. Sharp transport variance theory treats static complete or stratified randomization and ordinary empirical marginals.
